what: Wise moves money across borders. It holds local bank accounts in dozens of countries so a transfer never actually crosses a border, which makes it far cheaper than a bank wire, and it offers multi-currency accounts and cards.
customers: People sending money abroad, expatriates and migrants, and small businesses paying international suppliers.
money: the fee on moving money between currencies
moat: A network of local payment system connections built over a decade, which lets Wise settle domestically on both sides. Banks still route through correspondent chains that cost more.
risks: Wise cuts its own prices deliberately as volumes grow, so revenue grows more slowly than volume
Interest on customer balances is a large profit source and falls when rates fall
Payment regulators in several countries are reviewing how customer funds are held
opportunities: A 19.9% net margin and $32.4B of customer balances, with only $484M of debt
Revenue grew from $1.8B to $2.5B in two years
Analysts see about 60% upside, with 13 covering the stock, and the business-payments side is growing faster than consumer
watch: Cross-border volume growth and the take rate, which falls by design.
